findings.trigger: Valid restricted bearer, known active privileged actor ID, alternate casing of JSON ActorUserId field on body-authorized route.
findings.root_cause: Case-sensitive JsonElement field check disagrees with web case-insensitive DTO binding; handlers authorize request actor instead of bearer actor.
findings.impact: Possible privileged permission grants and false actor attribution within target/permission constraints; no anonymous bypass asserted.
findings.recommendation: Bind command actor exclusively to authenticated context; reject inconsistent/duplicate actor representations as defense in depth. No fix applied.
required_regression_tests: Restricted versus privileged real fixture actors through full Minimal API pipeline
No writable live database used for validation
findings.remaining_uncertainty: Real HTTP transport and DB permission mutation not executed. Full188endpoint authorization impact and non-JSON binding cases not exhaustively traced. Ten isolated binding/middleware controls pass.

findings.title: PIN-bearing user-management requests are durably stored as unencrypted JSON
evidence_chain: App constructor configures actual cashier file store before view-model field initializers.
Users action DTO carries InitialPin or CurrentPin/NewPin; durable owner keys users.create and users.change-pin are explicit.
RetainedRequest.SendAsync persists first unresolved DTO before transport; ambiguous outcome retains the exact object.
FileRetainedRequestStore.Save serializes Payload=request without exclusion or encryption, writes plain text temp, then moves to station LocalApplicationData JSON.
preconditions: Actual user-management operation with PIN-bearing fields and working durable store.
Access to the Windows profile journal, its filesystem copies/backup, or another permitted local collection mechanism while data remains.
counterevidence: Windows profile ACLs constrain access; no ACL deficiency demonstrated.
First known result, including definite initial rejection, clears the journal; known successful resolution clears recovered records.
Unwritable persistence may leave no file; observed source behavior is not proof every real station has exposed records.
Separate station directories reduce cross-client mixing but are not credential encryption.
findings.impact: Credential values may survive transient UI entry in local unencrypted recovery state; no unauthenticated remote disclosure, arbitrary login or server PIN hash weakness established.

independent_verification.scope: Local plaintext serialization confirmed; actual deployment exposure and ACL access unverified

findings.recommendation: Design credential-free durable recovery/status using server-owned request identity; minimize secret retention. If unavoidable, choose approved per-user protected storage and explicit lifecycle, but encryption alone does not replace recovery design. No fix implemented.
required_regression_tests: In-memory fake-store serialization tests asserting all PIN values absent from durable representations.
Create/change PIN known success, known initial failure, ambiguous timeout and recovered success without secret persistence.
User/station identity scoping, migration of preexisting journals only through explicitly authorized safe handling.
regression_risks: Removing recovery fields without protocol change could strand ambiguous account creation/change or cause repeated credential changes.
findings.remaining_uncertainty: No actual journal, credential, filesystem ACL or deployed backup collected. Independent source challenge and owner retention policy remain pending.
findings.additional_source_observation: If temporary write succeeds but File.Move fails, exception is swallowed; Clear removes only main JSON. A leftover temp can retain same plaintext. No actual leftover file observed.
